messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: prod.gateway high 5xx rate detected (5xx spike > 5% over 3m). Auto-escalate to #incidents.

oncall-bot: Alert details: gateway/errors=6.2% 3m, avg latency 1.8s, tail p99 12s. Affected route: /v1/generate (hosted).

jordan: I'm on it, paging from US-west. Seeing a lot of gateway timeouts and 503s. Can someone check scheduler queue depth?

maria: grabbing scheduler dashboards now. Queue depth jumped ~x15 in last 6min. Many batches stuck in PREPARE state. HOL visible on scheduler-2.

samir: logs show KV cache growth on scheduler-2 host-3 (kv_cache_size MB rising). Could be memory pressure and preemptions causing long prep times.

jordan: customer impact? any big tenants hit?

liz: initial slice: traffic routing shows high retries for one enterprise tenant (acme-inc), but generic traffic also sees elevated latencies. Error budget for hosted tier approaching 3xx mgmt threshold.

eng-sre: hypothesis: sudden request pattern -> large prefix share -> KV-cache growth -> batch prep stalls -> HOL blocking -> other requests time out at gateway.

ops-bot: Running mitigation suggestion: 1) short-term: redirect a portion of traffic to secondary region; 2) evict long-running batches on scheduler-2; 3) scale up dedicated worker pool.

jordan: doing live mitigation step 2 first — evict slow batches on scheduler-2 to break HOL. Command:

```
# evict long prepare batches older than 30s on scheduler-2
./bin/schedulerctl evict --host scheduler-2 --age 30s --reason "live-mitigation HOL"
```

maria: running it now.

maria: output: evicted 42 batches, reclaimed 1.6GB KV, some backpressure relieved. Queue depth decreased ~40% in 30s.

samir: good. I'm also bumping serving pool by +2 nodes in us-west-1 to absorb in-flight.

jordan: doing a controlled reroute of 20% traffic away from us-west to eu-west to ease scheduling pressure.

liz: alerting CSE: "We're mitigating a scheduling backlog causing 5xx/timeouts; we've evicted stuck batches, scaled serving, and rerouted traffic. Monitoring for 10m to confirm."

eng-sre: watching error rate. p95 dropped from 4.1s -> 1.9s after evictions, 5xx rate down to 3.2%. Still above baseline.

maria: digging into why KV-cache blew up. Found a spike of long-context requests from a small subset of clients that hit the same model shard, causing cache miss churn and large KV allocations.

samir: can we enable per-client prefix throttling to prevent large contiguous KV allocations?

jordan: can we patch quick throttle rule? ops-bot can you apply policy?

ops-bot: Applying a temporary rate-limit rule:
```
--policy-id temp-prefix-throttle-174900
match: route=/v1/generate, header:X-Customer-ID in [acme-inc-heavy]
action: limit concurrent=4 per-key window=60s
```
Applied.

liz: after throttle applied, second wave of KV growth stopped. 5xx now 1.1% and p99 dropped to 3.2s. Still monitoring.

jordan: next steps: 1) continue monitoring for 20m, 2) run postmortem triage when stable, 3) notify affected accounts and list mitigation timeline. Who will own postmortem?

samir: I'll lead the tech postmortem (root cause: KV-cache growth + HOL blocking + insufficient preemption).

liz: I'll take customer comms and coordinate with CSE. Draft note: short summary, actions taken, impact window, mitigation steps and follow-ups.

maria: action item: write a scheduler hard-timeout for PREPARE state > 45s to auto-evict to avoid HOL next time. I can PR tonight.

eng-sre: action item: add a metric for per-client KV allocation and an alert when a single client exceeds 30% of shard KV for >1m.

jordan: thanks. Current status: errors falling, routing steady. Will keep this thread updated. If anyone sees new regression ping me.

ops-bot: Incident timeline (brief):
- 1749001200: initial 5xx spike detected by alerting.
- 1749001234: thread created and paging started.
- 1749001250: evicted 42 batches on scheduler-2.
- 1749001275: +2 serving nodes in us-west applied.
- 1749001310: 20% traffic reroute to eu-west.
- 1749001350: temporary per-client throttle policy applied.
- 1749001420: 5xx rate reduced to ~1.1%.

jordan: marking mitigations done for now. Leaving incident open for postmortem and follow-ups.

maria: will open PR for PREPARE timeout and add unit tests. Link: https://git.redwood/infracode/pulls/2784 (will update when created).

samir: I'll schedule a deep-dive runbook update — include guidance for KV-cache runaway patterns and eviction playbook.

liz: CSE notified customers impacted between 1749001200-1749001420, included details and ETA for follow-up.

eng-sre: final note: Root cause summary for postmortem: concentrated long-context traffic to single shard -> KV-cache growth -> batch preparation stalls on scheduler-2 -> head-of-line blocking -> gateway timeouts. Mitigations: temporary throttling, evictions, scale-up, reroute. Long-term: per-client KV limits, PREPARE hard-timeout, improved autoscaling for scheduler-prep.

jordan: thanks all — great rapid ops. I'll close this thread after postmortem items are in tracker."
